claims.statement: src/struts.xml declares no <action>, <result> or <interceptor-stack> element for business endpoints: it only sets two constants and the basicstruts package, so every one of the 47 endpoint URLs and all 36 result names in the application exist only as @Action/@Result annotation strings on the action classes and as literals in JSPs, with no XML or other file duplicating them.

The application exposes 47 @Action endpoints in eight classes under src/com/caozhihu/tmall/action/: 24 on ForeAction (fore...) and 23 split over CategoryAction, ProductAction, ProductImageAction, PropertyAction, PropertyValueAction, UserAction and OrderAction (admin_...).

@Action's value string is the complete URL (not a class-name-derived name) because Action4Result carries @Namespace("/") and @ParentPackage("basicstruts") for all eight action classes, and every method passes an explicit value.

All three custom interceptors decide whether to act by testing the request URI with startsWith("/fore"), so a storefront endpoint renamed to a path that no longer begins with /fore keeps working but silently loses the auth gate, the cs category list and the cart item counter, and the admin_* family is never inspected at all.

AuthInterceptor's noNeedAuthPage array holds eight names (home, checkLogin, register, loginAjax, login, product, category, search) that are compared against StringUtils.substringAfterLast(uri, "/fore") - the tail of the @Action value, not the URL and not the Java method name - so renaming a public fore endpoint's @Action value withholds anonymous access (302 to login.jsp) and makes its AJAX callers receive the login page HTML instead of the success body.

AuthInterceptor tests the raw request URI without removing the servlet context path, while CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor and CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor both strip it first, so the three interceptors agree only while the application is deployed at the root context path the launcher sets.

Action4Result declares the shared result catalogue of 36 names - 26 dispatcher forwards and 10 redirect results - and every action method returns one of those names as a bare string, so a mistyped or renamed name affects all endpoints returning it and the action body has already executed before the failure surfaces.

Six of the ten redirect results carry OGNL parameters whose names must match setters on the receiving action and whose ${...} paths must match getters on the sending action: listPropertyPage -> /admin_property_list?category.id=${property.category.id}, listProductPage -> /admin_product_list?category.id=${product.category.id}, listProductImagePage -> /admin_productImage_list?product.id=${productImage.product.id}, buyPage -> forebuy?oiids=${oiid}, alipayPage -> forealipay?order.id=${order.id}&total=${total}, reviewPage -> forereview?order.id=${order.id}&showonly=${showonly}.

Redirect targets that dereference an association require the action to have populated it before the redirect renders, which is why handlers returning a Page result call t2p(...) first; t2p rebuilds the object from the database by id and reflects the setter name as "set" + class simple name.

An unbound parent filter fails differently per endpoint: BaseServiceImpl.list(Object... pairParams) converts a null value into Restrictions.isNull(key) and returns an empty list, whereas BaseServiceImpl.total(Object parent) calls parent.getClass() and Action4Service.t2p dereferences its argument, both failing with unchecked errors.

The only bindable request surface is the fields plus public setters on the Action4* chain (Action4Upload img/imgFileName/imgContentType, Action4Pagination page, Action4Pojo's nine entities and ten lists, Action4Parameter's msg/sort/contextPath/keyword/num/oiid/oiids/total/showonly); dotted names instantiate nested entities one level at a time, there is no per-action whitelist, and an unresolvable parameter name is ignored without an error.

The Action4Pojo property names double as the JSP EL names: fragments read ${categories}, ${products}, ${propertyValues}, ${orderItems} and dotted paths such as ${product.firstProductImage.id} through the getters of that class and of the entities, so renaming a field and its getter renders an empty fragment rather than failing.

Action4Parameter.contextPath is a bindable property that no code path ever sets, yet web/include/search.jsp and web/include/simpleSearch.jsp render ${contextPath} as a link target, so those two logo links currently resolve to the current URL and would change target if anyone invented a contextPath parameter.

All four multipart upload forms post the file under the field name img inside enctype="multipart/form-data" (listCategory.jsp and editCategory.jsp for category images, listProductImage.jsp twice for the single and detail panels), bound to Action4Upload.img and read directly by Action4Service.saveWithJpg; imgFileName and imgContentType are bound but never read by any code.

Page.defaultCount = 5 is the only source of count in the running system because the sole pager fragment never emits page.count, and because getLast() and getTotalPage() divide and take the modulus by count, a request that binds page.count=0 makes the render fail arithmetically instead of showing an empty page.

The getter isHasPreviouse() (misspelled) is read only through ${!page.hasPreviouse} at two lines of web/include/admin/adminPage.jsp, so renaming the method removes the property those <c:if> tests depend on and stops computing the disabled state of the two "previous" links; whether JSP EL then errors or renders an empty test is not settled by the repository.

Page.param is the filter suffix that keeps a paged admin list on its parent filter: it is written only by ProductAction.list and PropertyAction.list as "&category.id=" + id, and adminPage.jsp appends it raw after each ?page.start=... value, so a changed name or suffix shape makes the paging links drop the parent id and the next page reloads unbound.

Exactly four session attributes carry state across requests: user (written by ForeAction.login/loginAjax, removed by forelogout, read by AuthInterceptor, CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor, eight ForeAction methods and top.jsp), orderItems (written by ForeAction.buy, read by ForeAction.createOrder), cs (written by CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor on every /fore request, read by search.jsp and simpleSearch.jsp) and cartTotalItemNumber (written by CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor, read by top.jsp).

Renaming the session key user silently de-authenticates the application: the login action still redirects home but every protected /fore request is sent back to login.jsp, the top bar keeps rendering the login/register links, and the cart badge stays 0; renaming orderItems makes ForeAction.createOrder dereference a null list (ois.isEmpty()) instead of forwarding to login.jsp.

The order status values are Java constants on OrderService (waitPay, waitDelivery, waitConfirm, waitReview, finish, delete) that are duplicated as literals in JSP filters: boughtPage.jsp uses orderStatus="waitPay"/"waitDelivery"/"waitConfirm"/"waitReview" attributes plus <c:if test="${o.status=='...'}"> blocks, and admin listOrder.jsp tests ${o.status=='waitDelivery'}, so a rename desynchronises the stored column value from the rendered filters.

The AJAX success contract is the bare response body: web/success.jsp contains only the word "success" and web/fail.jsp only "fail", and client scripts compare the response text - imgAndInfo.jsp for forecheckLogin and foreaddCart, cartPage.jsp for forechangeOrderItem and foredeleteOrderItem, editPropertyValue.jsp for admin_propertyValue_update - so changing the page content makes every asynchronous interaction take its failure branch with no server error.

Every image the application writes is named after the saved row id with a .jpg extension, and the file name is only available because the row is persisted first and the @Id is @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY): CategoryAction.add/update build img/category/<category.id>.jpg, ProductImageAction.add builds img/productSingle/<productImage.id>.jpg or img/productDetail/<productImage.id>.jpg.

Action4Service.saveWithJpg copies the multipart temp file to the final path and then decodes and re-encodes that same path as JPEG through ImageUtil.change2jpg (AWT toolkit decode, PixelGrabber with forceRGB=true, a DirectColorModel without an alpha mask) plus ImageIO.write; it catches only IOException and prints the stack trace, and a null result from change2jpg or resizeImage reaches ImageIO.write as an unchecked IllegalArgumentException.

Only a type_single product image gets derivatives: ProductImageAction.add creates img/productSingle_small/<id>.jpg at 56x56 and img/productSingle_middle/<id>.jpg at 217x190 after calling getParentFile().mkdirs() on each target, and the raw directory branch is if/else, so type_detail and every unrecognised value land in img/productDetail.

ProductImageService.type_single and type_detail are the only two image-type values the code recognises, and the same two strings are written literally as hidden form inputs in web/admin/listProductImage.jsp and as the seeded productimage.type column values in src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql, so renaming a constant requires changing the JSP values and the seed rows with it.

ProductImageServiceImpl.setFirstProductImage is the only place that decides which image represents a product: it returns early if the transient field is already set, otherwise queries type_single images for the product and assigns element 0, which - because BaseServiceImpl.list appends Order.desc("id") - is the newest single image; it is called from ProductServiceImpl.fill(Category), ForeAction.product/search, ProductAction.list and OrderItemServiceImpl.fill(Order).

ImageUtil.resizeImage produces a straight stretch, never a crop: the in-memory overload allocates a BufferedImage of exactly the requested size with TYPE_INT_RGB and draws srcImage.getScaledInstance(width, height, Image.SCALE_SMOOTH) at 0,0, and the numbers 56, 217 and 190 appear only at the two ProductImageAction call sites (the markup sets no width/height for those images).

Every image URL in the JSPs is a relative path of the form <directory>/<id>.jpg composed from a row id: img/category/${c.id}.jpg in admin/listCategory.jsp and the category/product fragments, img/productSingle/${pi.id}.jpg in imgAndInfo.jsp and listProductImage.jsp, img/productSingle_small/${pi.id}.jpg only in imgAndInfo.jsp, img/productSingle_middle/${...firstProductImage.id}.jpg in the home/category/cart/buy/confirmPay fragments, img/productSingle/${p.firstProductImage.id}.jpg in productsBySearch.jsp, listProduct.jsp, listOrder.jsp and reviewPage.jsp, and img/productDetail/${pi.id}.jpg in productDetail.jsp and listProductImage.jsp.

A product with no type_single image renders a broken image rather than an error: firstProductImage stays null, so ${...firstProductImage.id} evaluates empty and the emitted URL collapses to img/productSingle/.jpg, which was never written.

Relative img/... and link URLs only resolve because a dispatcher forward keeps the action URL, and every action URL is at the context root because Action4Result declares @Namespace("/"); requesting a forwarded JSP by its own path (for example /admin/listCategory.jsp) re-bases the same relative URLs one level deeper and breaks the images.

src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql is executed at every Spring context refresh by the dbInit DataSourceInitializer bean referenced as classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql with UTF-8 encoding, and because StartJetty copies only non-.java resources found under src/ into web/WEB-INF/classes, any script referenced as classpath: must live under src/.

The seed script ends with five identity calibrations that pin post-seed ids to the original MySQL sequence: category RESTART WITH 84, product 963, productimage 10211, property 258, propertyvalue 14092; user, order_, review and orderitem are created without any rows or calibration, and for productimage the calibrated value (10211) is above the highest seeded id (10198).

The persistence layer's query vocabulary is built from class names and Java string literals rather than from a mapping file: BaseServiceImpl.total() composes "select count(*) from " + clazz.getName(), listByParent/list(Page,Object)/total(Object) derive the criteria property from StringUtils.uncapitalize(parent.getClass().getSimpleName()), and callers pass keys such as "product", "type", "user" and "order", so renaming an entity class or property requires editing those literals and fails only when the query is compiled.

The SessionFactory bean sf declares depends-on="dbInit" so the seed script runs before Hibernate initialises, and hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=none keeps Hibernate out of schema maintenance because the previous update value re-created the propertyvalue.pid foreign key that the seed data violates; the symptom of losing the ordering is a missing-table failure rather than a startup error.

The Spring wiring depends on bean names that code looks up by string: @Resource(name = "sf") in DAOImpl and @Resource(name = "dao") in ServiceDelegateDAO, transactionManager referenced by tx:annotation-driven, plus the component-scan base package com.caozhihu.tmall.* and packagesToScan com.caozhihu.* that decide which beans and entities exist at all.

src/struts.xml installs the application's interceptor chain through the package basicstruts, the stack name auth-dafault (matched on both the stack definition and the default-interceptor-ref) and three named interceptors whose class names are project classes, with the framework defaultStack last so it keeps performing parameter binding and multipart handling for every endpoint.

struts.objectFactory=spring is what lets every action and interceptor receive its @Autowired collaborators, and struts.i18n.encoding=UTF-8 is the second of the two UTF-8 declarations (web.xml also installs a CharacterEncodingFilter on /*).

StartJetty hard-codes the deployment constants PORT = 8080, H2_CONSOLE_PORT = 8082 and CONTEXT_PATH = "/", and the context path must stay "/" because every JSP link and src is relative to the context root and AuthInterceptor tests the unstripped request URI against "/fore".

The launcher pins seven class-name prefixes to the parent (system) class loader with addSystemClass and replaces the embedded Jetty Configuration chain with an explicit list that includes AnnotationConfiguration and JettyWebXmlConfiguration, because every jar is both on the JVM classpath and in WEB-INF/lib; dropping either produces the recorded JSP failures getTldCache() is null / TldCache cannot be cast.

The root path is served by an anonymous Jetty Rule that rewrites only the exact target "/" to "/forehome" because web/WEB-INF/web.xml declares no welcome-file-list and may not be edited; a RewritePatternRule with pattern "/" would be prefix/regex semantics and rewrite every path including /img/** to the home page, so all site images would be answered with HTML.

The H2 console is started as an independent server on port 8082 instead of being mounted inside the web application because the Struts2 filter is mapped to /* in web.xml, so an in-app /h2-console/* path answers "no action mapped".

StartJetty compiles every .java file under src/ with -source/-target 8 into web/WEB-INF/classes and then copies every non-.java file under src/ preserving relative paths, aborting main() before any port binds when compilation fails; web/WEB-INF/classes is git-ignored, so src/ is the only source of truth and test code is compiled and deployed with the business code.

The checked-in demo image set under web/img is tracked in version control (.gitignore excludes only build output, OS files, *.log and H2 file-database artifacts, not web/img) and lives in the same directories the upload endpoints write into: the seeded categories have web/img/category/<id>.jpg files, while orphan ids exist with no seeded row (category 1.png, 2, 6-12, 66, 70; productSingle 19, 21, 22; productDetail 17) and web/img/lunbo holds 1-5.jpg although carousel.jsp references only 1-4.

Only the <id>.jpg name shape is reachable by the application, so a committed file whose id has no seeded row is never requested by any screen and a seeded row whose file is missing renders a broken image with no server error; which side is authoritative when the row set and the file set disagree is stated nowhere in the repository.

Uploaded bytes are durable while their rows are not: the database is a pure in-memory H2 instance rebuilt from the seed script at every start, so an uploaded file survives as an untracked addition in a tracked directory, disappears from every screen after a restart, and can be overwritten by a later session that reuses the same calibrated id.
